title: navigator-safety AUTO-APPROVES destructive Bash commands: emits permissionDecision 'allow' on rm -rf / git push --force / DROP TABLE, bypassing the permission prompt it claims to reinforce

evidence.quote: * Does NOT block - existing hooks (git-memory-check, etc.) handle blocking.
lines.push('Ensure user has confirmed this operation.');

observe_how: Per Claude Code PreToolUse semantics (and the repo's own schemas.md allow|deny|ask contract), an explicit 'allow' from any PreToolUse hook bypasses the permission system entirely — the user confirmation dialog that would normally gate an un-allowlisted `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git push --force`, or `DROP TABLE` is suppressed, and permissionDecisionReason on 'allow' is shown to the user, NOT to Claude. So the hook that exists to surface destructive-command rules 'for Claude's consideration' instead (a) never reaches Claude and (b) actively removes the human gate for exactly the dangerous commands it matches. It is registered live on matcher Bash in repo .claude/settings.json lines 100-108. Fix: drop the permissionDecision entirely and emit the warning via exit-0 stdout JSON with no decision (or switch to 'ask' for the high-risk patterns).
telemetry: Reproduce: in a session where `rm -rf <dir>` is not allowlisted, observe no permission dialog appears because the hook returned allow.
